1	# Task 11: Polished car-paint object with clearcoat on a turntable
2	
3	Framework: Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, drawing into the existing canvas with id #app. Show a glossy, candy-red, car-paint finished object on a slowly rotating turntable in a dark showroom. Since no model files are provided, construct the object procedurally from smooth shapes, for example a rounded, streamlined capsule or bean body with a separate smooth cabin bump and four dark rubber wheel discs, or any other smooth body with clearly curved, large reflective panels. The paint must look like automotive paint: a deep coloured base layer with fine metallic flake sparkle, topped by a glossy clear coat that mirrors a studio environment (long soft-box strip reflections that bend over the curved panels). Add chrome trim, such as a thin ring or strip, and a dark glass or black cabin panel for contrast. The turntable is a circular platform with a subtle ring light or reflective floor on which the object is mirrored faintly. Use a dark background with two or three long strip lights above and to the sides, plus a faint cool rim light, so the reflections read as soft-box highlights. The platform rotates the object at about 20 degrees per second while the camera stays still at a low, slightly front-three-quarter angle with the whole object in frame. 2	
3	Read this first. 3	`material.custom({ glsl: { vertex, fragment } })` is the escape hatch for effects the
4	built-in materials do not cover (sky, water, energy, toon ramps). It has a colour
5	contract and three failure modes that cost real time on real GPUs. Chunk names and
6	signatures: `docs/api/glsl-chunks.md`.

8	## Colour contract
9	
10	- A custom shader writes **linear light**. The output stage always sRGB-encodes it,
11	  and the default ACES operator tones it down further, so a hex colour written
12	  straight to `outColor` comes out greyer than authored (a day sky read grey for
13	  exactly this reason). Post effects are not the cause: bloom, grade, vignette and
14	  fxaa leave a custom shader's colour unchanged.
15	- To show a hex colour as authored: `#include <colorspace_decode>`, wrap the colour
16	  in `a3dSrgbToLinear`, and set `output: { toneMapping: "none" }` on the app.
17	  `<colorspace_encode>` provides `a3dLinearToSrgb` for the other direction.
18	- Any other tone-mapping operator still tone-maps custom colours; tune the exposure
19	  instead of compensating in the shader.
